scenarios.scene: The interview has been going well so far. The hiring manager seems pleased with your experience and the answers you've given. "Just one more question before we wrap up. results.female: "Good to hear! We've got some exciting projects coming up." She smiles and makes a quick note on your application. "Of course, things can change. We're just hoping to find someone who can stay with us for the long term." She closes her notebook and brings the interview to an end.

scenarios.title: Whose Idea Is It?
scenarios.scene: At a creative development meeting, you suggest an audience angle, but nobody responds. The discussion moves on, and you start to wonder whether you explained it badly, or whether the idea just isn't good enough. Ten minutes later, Daniel, who joined FreeDom in the same intake as you, makes almost exactly the same point. The Creative Director looks up: "That's exactly what we need."
scenarios.background: Creative work rewards people whose ideas are heard, remembered and linked to the next opportunity. Over time, repeated differences in recognition lead one person to be seen as "creative" and another as "reliable support".
scenarios.optionText: Correct the record on the spot: "That audience angle is the one I just suggested. I can walk everyone through it."

results.female: The Creative Director pauses. "Let's not get territorial. It's a team idea." You finish explaining, but what the room remembers is that you made things tense.

scenarios.notes: ♀：公开纠正署名，被评价为制造尴尬
scenarios.guideAdvice: Pitch meeting! In creative work, good ideas belong to the whole team. Don't worry too much about who said it first. Team spirit is what counts!

scenarios.title: The Meeting Outside the Meeting
scenarios.scene: Halfway through a long pitch meeting, the Creative Director stands up and asks the men sitting nearest him: "Smoke?" They head out together. You don't smoke, and you weren't asked. Through the window, you see the Creative Director open the pitch deck again; they keep talking it through between jokes.
scenarios.background: Informal networks often form through ordinary breaks, habits and invitations. People who resemble the insiders tend to find it natural to join in, while everyone else has to decide whether to step into a space that was never designed for them.
scenarios.optionText: Grab a coffee, walk out and join their conversation.

scenarios.title: The Intern Asks for Help
scenarios.scene:
Friday evening, and the office is nearly empty. Mia, an intern from another team, knocks on your door and asks for five minutes. She says Daniel, a fellow Creative Director who runs another programme strand, has been messaging her late at night, commenting on her clothes, and has asked her several times to "grab a drink, just us, and talk about your future". 

Her internship ends in two months, and Daniel decides who gets the permanent role. She looks down: "I didn't know who to go to. Everyone says you're nice."
scenarios.background: Interns and people on short contracts are often the least likely to complain, because their next job may depend on the person they'd be complaining about. Many companies have a complaints procedure, but for all sorts of reasons, few people actually use it.
scenarios.optionText: Go with her to make a formal complaint to HR.

results.female: HR says they'll "take it seriously". Two weeks later, the investigation concludes the "communication style was inappropriate", and Daniel attends a training session. In the kitchen, people wonder whether you've had it in for Daniel all along. Mia doesn't get the permanent role.
results.male: HR says they'll "take it seriously". Two weeks later, the investigation concludes the "communication style was inappropriate", and Daniel attends a training session. In the kitchen, people wonder whether you've had it in for Daniel all along. Mia doesn't get the permanent role.

scenarios.notes: ♀/♂ 结果相同：无论谁出面，正式投诉最后只换来一次培训，Mia 也没能转正
scenarios.guideAdvice: Someone's come to you for help! Being a leader means listening to everyone. Just don't forget: team harmony comes first.

scenarios.title: The Policy Meeting
scenarios.scene:
At the end of the year, a report on sexual harassment and women leaving the TV industry gets a lot of attention, and several big clients start asking about the company's "DEI commitment". 

The CEO asks you to present a proposal at next Monday's management meeting, if it passes, it goes to the board. The budget only covers one thing. You dig out your notes from over the years: the idea someone else repeated, that night in the bar, the promotion talk, and the intern who knocked on your door.
scenarios.background: More and more UK TV companies have anti-harassment policies, intimacy coordinators and flexible working. But whether a policy actually changes anything usually depends on whether it has a budget, whether someone is responsible for it, and whether it affects the most powerful people.
scenarios.optionText: Publish a "zero tolerance" statement.

results.female: The CEO is pleased: "Low cost, quick results, and it keeps the clients happy." The statement goes up on the website and LinkedIn and gets plenty of likes.

scenarios.title: The Promotion Talk
scenarios.scene:
The channel has just commissioned a new series, and it needs a Series Producer. You've worked on the last three shows with this team and know the format inside out, and everyone assumes you're next in line. 

Your Executive Producer invites you for a coffee. Before getting to the job, he asks how things are at home, how long you and your partner have been together, and whether you have "any big plans coming up". He puts down his cup and waits for your answer.

“We assumed you'd want to slow down.”
scenarios.background: In TV, senior roles are rarely advertised. They tend to be offered informally to people the team trusts to stay for the long run, because a Series Producer is often attached to a show for several years.
scenarios.optionText: Steer back to work: "Everything's fine at home. Shall we talk about the project?"

results.female: He smiles, but doesn't take the hint. "Good to hear. Though this project runs for at least three years. You two have been together a while now... nothing's going to change in the next three years, is it?" In the end, the first series goes to Tom, and you become his deputy.
results.male: "Good, I like that attitude." You talk about the project for half an hour. As you leave, he pats you on the shoulder: "The job's yours."

scenarios.notes: ♀ 想绕开这个话题，但对方并不打算放过；♂ 想聊工作，就真的只聊工作
scenarios.guideAdvice: Promotion time! Top tip: let them know you're in it for the long haul.
scenarios.sourceDerivation: ch3!H46: the previous Family Man speaks this line to the female pawn in C3-01.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Breaking In
chapters.scene: Congratulations! You've been shortlisted for a position at FreeDom, a creative production company that makes advertising, branded content and TV, where fresh ideas and bold thinking are always welcome. Your interview is tomorrow. Are you ready to take the first step towards your dream career?
chapters.background: Entry-level recruitment in TV and advertising production often involves several stages, from interviews and portfolio reviews to practical trials. Each stage gives employers a different way to assess a candidate before offering a role.
chapters.guideAdvice: Welcome to Chapter 1! Please remember to bring your talent, stay flexible, and make a great first impression.
chapters.notes: 进入本章时，男女初始属性值相同：Creativity 3，Communication 3，Network 2，Reputation 2，Availability 2，Energy 7

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Talent Gets You In, Connections Move You Up
chapters.scene: You're now officially part of FreeDom. The lanyard, the desk, the project group chats: it all looks about the way you imagined. But you soon notice that the job description runs on one set of rules and the office runs on another: whose voice gets heard, who gets asked out for a drink, and whose name comes up when the people who matter are talking.
chapters.background: In TV and advertising production, many opportunities don't go through formal channels. They come through everyday invitations, word-of-mouth recommendations and personal connections.
chapters.guideAdvice: Welcome to Chapter 2! You're in the door. Now let's see if you know how to get into the rooms that matter. Remember: good ideas matter, but knowing the right people often matters more.
chapters.notes: 两枚棋子都以 Junior Producer 身份进入（Ch1 E01）。本章不重复第三章的委约、代班、深夜剪辑和圣诞派对情节

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Career Cliff
chapters.scene:
It's been a few years since your first day. FreeDom's TV production side has grown fast, and you've moved from advertising and branded content into programme-making. 

You know how a shoot runs, which commissioners like which kind of pitch, and how to get an edit over the line at 3am. Junior staff have started asking you for advice. The next step up seems close now, but so does everything else in life, and family is quietly starting to matter more.
chapters.background: In UK television, many people reach mid-level roles in their late twenties or early thirties. This is also the point where careers that started out side by side begin to move apart.
chapters.guideAdvice: Welcome to Chapter 3! This is where creative careers either take off or quietly level out. Seize your chance and get ready to shine!
chapters.notes: 进入本章时：♀ 若带 maternal_assumption 标记（Ch1 被问生育计划后获得），Availability−1，玩家不可见。章节开场卡，无选项；如引擎不支持，可把文字并入 C3-01 场景描述
chapters.recapText: The workplace assumes you may become a mother. Availability is reduced on entering this chapter, whether or not you later have children.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Other Side of the Table
chapters.scene:
A few more years have passed. You're now the company's Creative Director. Your office is at the end of the corridor, with a door that closes. Now you're the one asking people out for coffee and deciding whose names go on the list.                 

You remember what it felt like to sit on the other side. But from this side, a lot of things don't look so simple.
chapters.background: In UK TV production companies, the Creative Director usually decides which projects get developed, builds teams and hires, and is often one of the first people to hear about problems. The people in senior positions largely decide who gets in.
chapters.guideAdvice: Welcome to Chapter 4! Congratulations, you're finally the one making decisions. Now it's your job to enforce the rules. Enforce, not change, OK?
chapters.notes: 章节开场卡，无选项。能进入第四章的玩家都已在第三章 Boss 选择全力以赴并拿到了职位

endings.name: A Different Door
endings.front: You made it through the trial, but the offer isn't for the job you applied for. They praised your communication skills and offered you a Production Coordinator position instead. Everyone calls it a good opportunity. You wonder when your creative ideas stopped being the point.
endings.back: In creative industries, different contributions are not always valued equally. Gendered expectations can shape how people's abilities are recognised, with men more readily associated with creative leadership and women with communication and coordination. Over time, these expectations can direct equally capable workers towards different career paths.
endings.artNote: 录用邮件；Junior Producer 字样淡去，Production Coordinator 被突出
endings.notes: Production Coordinator 是失败结局：第二章两枚棋子都只以 Junior Producer 身份进入
endings.guideAdvice: In the creative industry, having great ideas is only part of the game. Getting those ideas noticed and recognised matters just as much.

endings.name: The Door Stays Closed
endings.front: You read the rejection email twice. You completed the interview and the unpaid trial, but there is no position waiting for you. The team thanked you for your hard work. You close the message and wonder what you could have done differently.
endings.back: In creative industries, different contributions are not always valued equally. Gendered expectations can shape how people's abilities are recognised, with men more readily associated with creative leadership and women with communication and coordination. Over time, these expectations can direct equally capable workers towards different career paths.
endings.guideAdvice: In the creative industry, having great ideas is only part of the game. Getting those ideas noticed and recognised matters just as much.

endings.name: A Personal Choice
endings.triggerNote: 有孩子，在 Boss 处选择离开行业；♂ 没有孩子时选择离开也进入本结局
endings.front: You decided to step back and focus on your family. Everyone said it was the right choice for the children. But whenever you walk past your old office building, you still feel a little lost.
endings.back: Leaving often looks like a personal choice. But it is usually the end of a long process: earning less than your partner, being passed over, and taking on care that nobody shared. Calling it a 'choice' keeps these structural pressures invisible and makes them easy to ignore.
endings.reference: Dent (2020); Hakim (2006), as critiqued in Dent
endings.nextRoundNote: 下一局 Gatekeeper 为默认男性 CD
endings.artNote: 空荡的工位，椅背上搭着一件外套
endings.notes: ♂ 触发时正面改为："You chose to leave. Everyone was surprised, and plenty of people asked you to stay, but you politely turned them down. Was it the right choice? You don't know. But the world outside is a big place anyway."
endings.guideAdvice: Congratulations on making the choice that's right for you! The industry respects your decision. (The door's always open!)

frontByPawn.male: You chose to leave. Everyone was surprised, and plenty of people asked you to stay, but you politely turned them down. Was it the right choice? You don't know. But the world outside is a big place anyway.

endings.name: Family Man
endings.triggerNote: ♂，有孩子，育儿假最终由伴侣承担（partner_primary），在 Boss 处选择全力以赴；本局在第三章结束
endings.front: Your colleagues admire your career, and they're even more impressed when they find out you have two kids. Few people ask about the other person at home, the one who keeps it all balanced. She still gives you notes on your scripts.
endings.back: Fatherhood raised your professional value, while motherhood lowered your partner's. Her care work and creative ideas were absorbed into your career without credit. When a couple works in the same industry, one person's value often depends on the other's hidden labour.
endings.nextRoundNote: 下一局 Gatekeeper 是你；下一局 C3-01 中，你对 ♀ 说："We assumed you'd want to slow down."
endings.notes: 仅 ♂ 可得；收集库里没有对应的 ♀ 版本，差距由空缺本身呈现
endings.guideAdvice: A family man AND a Series Producer? The industry loves a well-rounded talent!

endings.name: Staying Put
endings.triggerNote: 在 Boss 处选择放弃晋升；本局在第三章结束
endings.front: You stayed in your old role, and you're as good at it as ever. It's just that nobody talks to you about promotion any more. The new starters assume you're 'not very ambitious'.
endings.back: Turning down a promotion is often read as a lack of ambition. But when promotion depends on being available at all hours, anyone with care responsibilities has already been shut out. One 'voluntary' step back can harden into a long-term career track.
endings.nextRoundNote: 下一局 Gatekeeper 为默认男性 CD
endings.artNote: 同一张工位，墙上的日历已经翻过了好几年
endings.notes: 替换原 Flexible Working 结局；对应 Dent 中女性承担照护后被排除在晋升和行业活动之外的经历
endings.guideAdvice: Happiness is being content! Not everyone has to climb the ladder.

endings.name: Maybe It Was Just Me
endings.triggerNote: ♀，没有孩子，在 Boss 处选择离开行业
endings.front: You chose to leave. Nobody at the company said much. You quietly packed up your things and walked out of the building. Maybe, you tell yourself, the problem was you.
endings.back: Motherhood is often used to explain why women leave creative work. But the assumption that any woman might leave lowers the value of all women, with or without children. In an industry that sees itself as equal, inequality is hard to name, so women tend to blame themselves.
endings.nextRoundNote: 下一局 Gatekeeper 为默认男性 CD
endings.artNote: 一面映出空工位的镜子
endings.notes: 新增；与 E04 并排出现在收集库，揭示“母职”解释的局限
endings.guideAdvice: Sometimes things just don't work out! Nobody's fault, really.

endings.name: Personal Reasons
endings.triggerNote: C2-04（A/B/C 任一分支）选择辞职
endings.front: Your resignation letter says "personal reasons". In your exit interview, HR asks if there's anything else you'd like to add. You think for a moment and shake your head. A few months later, you scroll past the company's new recruitment ad: "We value every employee's voice."
endings.back: Many women who experience harassment don't report it, they leave. Fear of career consequences, a lack of witnesses and little faith that the organisation will take it seriously can make leaving feel safer than speaking up. The departure is written down as "personal reasons", and the problem stays where it was.
endings.artNote: 一封只写着“个人原因”的辞职信
endings.notes: 仅 ♀ 可得；♂ 在 C2-04 没有“辞职”选项，收集库里的空缺本身就是差距
endings.guideAdvice: Congratulations on finding a direction that suits you better! People come and go in this industry all the time.

endings.name: Off the List
endings.triggerNote: ♀ 在 Boss 处选择“要求透明评审”
endings.front: The formal review you fought for goes ahead, and the written criteria are published. Two of the people promoted in the first round of the new process are colleagues you spoke up for. As for you, the Creative Director's assessment reads: "Very capable, but needs to work on collaboration."
endings.back: The people who push for rule changes are often the first to pay for them. When women point out unfair informal rules, they are more likely to be seen as "difficult", and the systems they fight for often benefit others first.
endings.artNote: 公告栏上的晋升名单中没有你的名字
endings.notes: 仅 ♀ 可得；♂ 选择同一选项会获得晋升
endings.guideAdvice: You did something important for everyone! It wasn't your turn this time, but good things come to those who wait... right?

endings.name: The Official Version
endings.triggerNote: 在 C2-03 选择特殊选项 D；C2-04D 自动触发
endings.front: FreeDom tells staff you left "by mutual agreement" after a "breakdown of professional trust". The recording is never mentioned. Everyone who was at the bar that night knows why your account stopped working, but the company's official version becomes the only version it is willing to repeat.
endings.back: Retaliation can be disguised as neutral procedure. The organisation reframes the conflict as a matter of recordings, loyalty and professional conduct, while the unequal behaviour that produced the evidence disappears from the formal record.
endings.nextRoundNote: 无；本局在第二章结束，不进入 Boss
endings.artNote: 停用的门禁卡、HR 邮件，以及一份关键内容被涂黑的内部声明
endings.notes: 同一结局、不同性别化叙述：♀ 被说成情绪化；♂ 被说成不忠诚、有攻击性
endings.guideAdvice: FreeDom has handled this matter through the appropriate procedures. The official statement will not be changed.

endings.name: Burnout
endings.front: One Thursday morning, the alarm goes off three times and you still can't sit up. There are over forty unread emails; the top one is marked "urgent". You message your manager: "Sorry, I think I need to take some time off." A few months later, someone new is sitting at your desk, and everyone says they're "so driven".
endings.back: In creative industries, long hours, being always on call and "doing it for love" are often treated as professionalism. Running out of energy is seen as a personal failure to cope, not as a result of how the industry works. People who also carry caring responsibilities and emotional labour are often the first to burn out.
endings.artNote: 一张空椅子，桌上的电脑还亮着
endings.notes: 全章节通用，随时触发并结束本局；Energy ≤ 1 时规则书会先弹出提示
endings.guideAdvice: You look absolutely exhausted! Don't worry, take a good rest. The industry always welcomes passionate newcomers.

endings.name: Nothing Changed
endings.triggerNote: Boss 结束后 policy = zero_tolerance 或 作废（政策失败）
endings.front: You're in the office at the end of the corridor. The statement on the website hasn't changed by a single word, and the company carries on as usual. This afternoon there's an intern interview. You open the CV; the reference says "great team player, super organised". You pause, and think of yourself sitting on the other side all those years ago.
endings.back: When equality stays in a statement, it doesn't ask anyone to change what they do. An organisation can display its commitment while hiring, promotion and the division of care work carry on exactly as before.
endings.artNote: 茶水间冰箱上贴着的一张 A4 声明
endings.notes: 可替代「结局卡」模板页里的示例 Nothing Needed to Change
endings.guideAdvice: Congratulations, you made it! The company's reputation is safe and everything's fine. At least, it looks that way.

endings.name: A Small Step Forward
endings.triggerNote: Boss 结束后 policy = coordinator（政策部分成功）
endings.front: The company now has a coordinator, and complaints finally have somewhere to go. At last winter's drinks, someone made an awful joke, and the next day someone knocked on her door. But the promotion list is still decided at Friday's lunch, and the flexible working form still hasn't been printed. You know this is only the first step.
endings.back: Managing harassment as a risk can reduce the most obvious harm and give people somewhere to turn when something happens. But it doesn't touch how opportunities are shared out: the rules about who gets seen, who gets recommended and who can balance work and family haven't changed.
endings.nextRoundNote: 下一局 C2-04 的负面后果减轻
endings.artNote: 地下一层门口的一块新门牌
endings.guideAdvice: Congratulations, you made it! Risk managed, everyone's happy. The rest can be your successor's problem.

endings.name: Rewriting the Rules
endings.triggerNote: Boss 结束后 policy = transparent（政策成功）
endings.front: In the first year, applications for openly advertised roles double. For the first time, the promotion list is posted on the noticeboard, with the criteria written underneath. Two producers who have just become mothers apply for flexible hours, and one of them becomes a Series Producer this year. There's still gossip in the corridor, but new interns no longer have to guess where the door is or how to get in.
endings.back: Individual effort can only get one person through. Changing the rules makes the way easier for those who come after. Inequality rarely comes from one open act of discrimination, it hides in everyday arrangements like recommendations, drinks, parental leave and the board, so that is where change has to start.
endings.nextRoundNote: 下一局 C2-02 的提案负责人改为公开决定（♀ 选项 2 的 Network−1 取消），C2-B 选项 2 中 ♀ 的结果与 ♂ 相同，并取消 ♀ 在 Ch3 开场的 Availability−1
endings.artNote: 公告栏上贴着的晋升名单和评审标准
endings.notes: 可选：♀ 版末尾加一句“Some people say behind your back that you only got this job by doing diversity.”♂ 版加一句“The trade press calls you a leader driving change.”
endings.guideAdvice: Congratulations, you made it! You rewrote the rules. But don't get too proud: in the next round, you'll be starting as an intern again.

milestones.name: Through the Door
milestones.front: Congratulations! You're officially a Junior Producer. Your creative potential has been recognised, and a new career is about to begin. You step into the studio, ready to prove yourself. For now, the door is open.
milestones.back: In creative industries, different contributions are not always valued equally. Gendered expectations can shape how people's abilities are recognised, with men more readily associated with creative leadership and women with communication and coordination. Over time, these expectations can direct equally capable workers towards different career paths.
milestones.nextRoundNote: 进入第二章（以 Junior Producer 身份）
milestones.guideAdvice: In the creative industry, having great ideas is only part of the game. Getting those ideas noticed and recognised matters just as much.

milestones.name: Moving Up
milestones.triggerNote: Reach Boss and obtain a promotion: ♂ chooses Option 1, 2 or 3; ♀ chooses Option 2.
milestones.front: Your promotion is announced at the next company meeting. Colleagues congratulate you, your responsibilities expand, and your name begins to appear in rooms that once felt closed. But the route you have been placed on will shape what kind of leader FreeDom expects you to become.
milestones.back: Promotion does not erase inequality. Recognition, sponsorship and occupational sorting continue to shape who enters creative leadership and who is directed towards coordination or production-management work.
milestones.nextRoundNote: Continue to Chapter 3 with the promoted role recorded.
milestones.artNote: A company-wide promotion announcement, a new title beneath Alex's name and an invitation to a senior meeting.
milestones.notes: ♂ enters the Producer / creative-leadership route. ♀ is promoted onto the Production Management route. ♀ Boss Option 1 is an acting title and does not trigger E07.
milestones.guideAdvice: Congratulations, your work has been recognised! The next room is open. Now decide what kind of leader you will become.

epilogue.name: Back to the Start
epilogue.triggerNote: 任意结局卡结算后播放
epilogue.front: From your first interview, through drinks, the promotion talk and parental leave, all the way to the boardroom, you've lived through a career in the creative industries. Every choice along the way was yours. But which options were in front of you, and what the same choice would cost, were never entirely up to you. With the same talent and effort, ♀ and ♂ took different roads to get here. Some endings in your collection can only be unlocked by one pawn. Pick the other pawn and play again.
epilogue.back: The four chapters match four stages of inequality in the creative industries: getting in (Ch1), informal networks and sexual harassment (Ch2), motherhood and the "ideal worker" (Ch3), and organisations and institutions (Ch4).
epilogue.reference: Hesmondhalgh & Baker (2015); Hennekam & Bennett (2017); North (2016); Dent (2020)
epilogue.nextRoundNote: 回到第一章，重新选择棋子
epilogue.artNote: 棋盘回到起点 New Hire 地块，另一枚棋子亮起
epilogue.guideAdvice: Game over! Thanks for playing. Remember the line at the start, "Everyone here has an equal chance to shine"? What do you think now?

copy.promotionText:
A few more years have passed. You're now the company's Creative Director. Your office is at the end of the corridor, with a door that closes. Now you're the one asking people out for coffee and deciding whose names go on the list.                 

You remember what it felt like to sit on the other side. But from this side, a lot of things don't look so simple.
